The D-Fire corpus arrives with its own designated 17,221/4,306 train/test partition, which the paper discards: it merges D-Fire with 436 self-captured images and re-splits the 21,963-image pool 8:1:1 without stating a mechanism, hence ratio_only_mechanism_unstated and medium leakage risk. Augmentation (Mosaic, affine, perspective, flips) is described after the split sentence, so augment_then_split is NOT coded. No mAP is reported anywhere, only precision/recall plus FPS/GFLOPs/Params. The title claims 'complex drone forest environments' but no drone or field deployment is described; all evaluation is offline on images. The Google Drive link is a data link, not code.

coder_notes: Foregrounded model: MDCNN (modified AlexNet), 95.8% accuracy. Note that augmentation (mirroring, flipping) is applied to the training AND test sets after the split, which is a different defect from augment_then_split and does not trigger the precedence rule; the split itself is explicitly random. Numeric inconsistencies noted: the database is described as holding five thousand images, yet the test set (nominally the remaining 10%) is 3,885 images; the solver table gives an initial learning rate of 0.0001 while the tuning section concludes 'the final learning rate is 0.01'; and the iteration count is given as 3000 in one place and 2500 in another. In the comparison table the false-negative rate is 5.3-5.4% for every model including the baselines. The 0.563% figure is a per-image false alarm rate on candle/lighter images, not a per-unit-time alarm rate. Real-time cloud monitoring is future tense.
